data.Name: Check here if you are married.

Enter your personal information here:
Enter your Spouse's personal information here:
Enter personal information for any and all children here (i.e., all of your children, and all of your Spouse's children if you are married).

If you want to name anyone else in your documents, enter their information here. These can be people or entities. For example, you may want to have your niece serve as the Executor of your Will, and leave half of your estate to her and half to a charity. You would enter both your niece's information and the charity's information in this section, but as separate entries.

Choose your initial Executors (the people you want to manage the distribution of your estate after you have passed). Everyone selected in this list will serve together as Co-Executors. If you are married, usually people choose their spouse as their first and sole initial Executor.
Select the person you want to serve as your first agent:
If you want a Co-Agent to serve with your first agent, select them here:
Check here if you want to appoint successor agents to fill in if the agents above can't or won't be your agent.
Select your successor agents here:
Check here if you wish to be an organ donor.

Select the person you want to fill this role:

Check here if you want the two people above to be able to make decisions independently, without having to agree.
Check here if you want the two people above (your initial agents) to be able to make decisions independently, without having to agree.

Select the owner of the property - if this is property that you or your spouse inherited or owned prior to your marriage, select the person who inherited or owned it; otherwise, for all property acquired during your marriage, select the "jointly" option.
Who are this child's parents?

Check here if your Spouse wants to appoint successor agents to fill in as your Spouse's Healthcare agent if the people above can't or won't be your Spouse's agent.
Check here if you want to appoint successor agents to fill in as your Financial agent if the people above can't or won't be your agent.

Select the successor agents for your Healthcare Power of Attorney here:
Select the successor agents for your Spouse's Financial Power of Attorney here:
Select the successor agents for your Financial Power of Attorney here:

Select the person you want to serve as your first agent for your Financial Power of Attorney:
Select the person your Spouse wants to serve as the first agent for your Spouse's Financial Power of Attorney:
Select the person you want to serve as your first agent for your Healthcare Power of Attorney:
Select the person your Spouse wants to serve as the first agent for your Spouse's Healthcare Power of Attorney:
Select the Tutor for your minor children below - this is the first person who will care for your children if they are minors when you pass away.
Select the Under-Tutor for your minor children below - this is the  person who will care for your children if your Tutor is not able to care for them.
Do you have minor children? If so, below you will select a Tutor and an Under-Tutor to care for your children if you pass away while they are still minors.

Do you want to gift specific property (personal items, vehicles, a house or land, etc) when you pass away? Any property not specifically given to a person (or entity) will be divided among the residual beneficiaries you will enter below.
Enter information on the gifts of specific property here - you will select the beneficiary and describe the property you want to give them.

Enter how much of your estate this beneficiary should get; whatever you type in will come into the document, so enter this in either fractions or a percent, like the following examples: "1/3" or "60%". Try to be consistent across all your beneficiaries, and make sure the total adds up to your full estate (i.e., the fractions add up to 1 or the percents add up to 100%). For example, if you have three beneficiaries that you want to divide your estate equally between, you would enter "1/3" for each of them. If you have four beneficiaries with unequal amounts, you might enter "20%" for the first beneficiary, "20%" for the second beneficiary, "10%" for the third beneficiary, and "50%" for the fourth beneficiary.

Describe the property you want to give this person. Be specific - you want to fill in the brackets in this sentence: "my Executor shall distribute [property being given] to this recipient". For example, if you want to give this person your motorcycle, you would type in "my red Harley-Davidson motorcycle", or even "my red Harley-Davidson motorcycle, license plate 3W3-ZE8". You need to be specific enough that there is no question about what property you are giving this person.

You (and your spouse, if you are married) will be your own initial Trustee(s). Select here the people or entities you want to be your successor Trustees when you (or your Spouse) is no longer able to serve as Trustee.
Check here if you (or your Spouse, if you are married) want to leave specific property (a home, a car, jewelry, etc) to a person or entity in your Trust.
Enter information about your and your Spouse's specific bequests below.
Enter information about your specific bequests below.
Check here if you want to disinherit this child - in other words, if you want to specifically say that they will not receive any of your estate.
Check here if this person has passed away.
Check here if you (or your Spouse, if you are married) have any prior marriages.

If you are in a terminal and irreversible condition certified by two physicians to be the end of life stage, what is the maximum number of days (between zero and 30 days) you wish to be kept alive by life-sustaining procedures that only serve to prolong artificially the dying process?  For example, if you select 15 days, your attending physician will employ artificial life-sustaining treatment or procedures for 15 days, but if you do not show improvement within that time period, your instructions will direct that life-sustaining procedures be withdrawn so that you may be allowed to die naturally.

If your Spouse is in a terminal and irreversible condition certified by two physicians to be the end of life stage, what is the maximum number of days (between zero and 30 days) your Spouse wishes to be kept alive by life-sustaining procedures that only serve to prolong artificially the dying process?  For example, if you select 15 days, your Spouse's attending physician will employ artificial life-sustaining treatment or procedures for 15 days, but if your Spouse does not show improvement within that time period, your Spouse's instructions will direct that life-sustaining procedures be withdrawn so that your Spouse may be allowed to die naturally.

(Choose all that apply): Indicate which of the following specific treatments and procedures you wish to have your caretakers CONTINUE in the event two (2) physicians certify that you are in a terminal and irreversible condition and that your death will occur whether or not life-sustaining procedures are utilized to artificially prolong your life:

(Choose all that apply): Indicate which of the following specific treatments and procedures your Spouse wishes to have their caretakers CONTINUE in the event two (2) physicians certify that your Spouse is in a terminal and irreversible condition and that your Spouse's death will occur whether or not life-sustaining procedures are utilized to artificially prolong your Spouse's life:
Select whether this bequest should be given if you pass away first, if your spouse passes away first, or only once both of you have passed away.
Choose your successor Executors (the people you want to manage the distribution of your estate after your initial Executors are unable to serve).
Enter yourself and your adult child's other parent here; if there is anyone else who will serve as an agent for your adult child, enter them here as well.
